idea: VocacionData AI: orientacion vocacional basada en datos laborales reales para postulantes y estudiantes peruanos, usando un agente conversacional que cruza intereses, salarios, empleabilidad, oferta universitaria y ubicacion para reducir malas decisiones de carrera.
market: Peru: ~1 million students in last year of high school and ~500,000 university applicants annually. TAM: $50M (career guidance market, including test prep and counseling). SAM: $10M (digital career guidance tools). SOM: $1M (first 12 months, targeting 10,000 paid users at $100/year).

solutions.name: PruébaT
solutions.observed_positioning: Free online career test for Mexican students; uses psychometric questions but no labor market data.

solutions.name: CareerExplorer (Sokanu)
solutions.observed_positioning: Comprehensive career test with detailed reports; subscription-based; US-focused, no Peru data.

solutions.name: MyNextMove (O*NET)
solutions.observed_positioning: Free tool based on O*NET database; US-centric, not tailored to Peru.

solutions.name: 16Personalities
solutions.observed_positioning: Popular personality test loosely linked to careers; generic, no local labor data.

solutions.name: Coursera Career Academy
solutions.observed_positioning: Skill-based career guidance; global, not Peru-specific, requires course enrollment.

solutions.name: LinkedIn Career Explorer
solutions.observed_positioning: Uses LinkedIn data for career paths; limited in Peru due to low penetration, no university integration.

solutions.name: Khan Academy Career Content
solutions.observed_positioning: Free videos on careers; no interactive assessment or local data.

solutions.name: University career counseling offices
solutions.observed_positioning: Manual, one-on-one; limited capacity, not scalable, no real-time labor data.

solutions.name: Private career counselors (coaches)
solutions.observed_positioning: Expensive ($50-200/session), not accessible to most students, no data-driven insights.

solutions.name: Government portals (e.g., Ponte en Carrera)
solutions.observed_positioning: Static data on salaries and employability; no interactive agent, poor user experience.

solutions.name: Test vocacionales online (e.g., Educaweb)
solutions.observed_positioning: Basic psychometric tests; often outdated, no integration with real labor market.

solutions.name: ChatGPT / generic AI chatbots
solutions.observed_positioning: Can answer career questions but lacks structured data on Peru, no personalized matching.

solutions.name: YouTube career advice channels
solutions.observed_positioning: Free but unstructured, no personalization, no data validation.

solutions.name: School guidance counselors
solutions.observed_positioning: Overworked, understaffed, often lack up-to-date labor market information.

solutions.name: Do nothing / family advice
solutions.observed_positioning: Most common alternative; leads to uninformed decisions, perpetuates mismatch.

research_summary: The Peruvian career guidance market is fragmented, with no dominant digital solution that combines psychometric assessment with real-time labor data (salaries, employability, university offerings, location). Existing alternatives are either generic (global tools like 16Personalities, CareerExplorer), static (government portals), expensive (private coaches), or informal (family advice). A conversational AI agent that integrates local labor data could address the pain of poor career decisions, which affect ~70% of Peruvian students who choose careers without market information. The main competition is the 'do nothing' option and manual counseling. Key moat: proprietary dataset of Peruvian labor market + university data, and a personalized agent that improves with usage.
